title: Nested pediatric low-grade glioma cerebral organoid avatars reveal glutamatergic neuron stromal growth dependency.
abstract: Pilocytic astrocytomas (PAs), the most common pediatric brain tumor, grow slowly and depend heavily on their local brain microenvironment, hindering accurate humanized model development. To surmount this barrier, we developed mixed assembloids of PAs nested within human iPSC-cerebral organoids (PANCOs) that recapitulate PA histopathology and growth. Consistent with their cell-intrinsic ERK dependence, MEK inhibition reduces PANCO proliferation, whereas clozapine-N-oxide-activatable neural progenitors integrate into PANCOs, preferentially differentiate into glutamatergic neurons, and increase cell-extrinsic PA proliferation, which is blocked by glutamate receptor inhibition. These accurate in vitro pediatric PA avatars provide tractable platforms to discover and validate PA cell-intrinsic and cell-extrinsic growth dependencies.
authors: Enquan Xu; Christina Zhang; Fausto J Rodriguez; Sonika Dahiya; Corina Anastasaki; David H Gutmann
methods: Materials and methods Human PA cells Operative specimens from children with NF1-associated and sporadic PA tumors were collected under an approved Human Studies (Institutional Review Board) protocol at Washington University School of Medicine and used to derive primary PA cells ( Anastasaki et al. 2025 ). These PA cells were maintained in tissue culture-treated, uncoated, and vented T75 flasks in DMEM supplemented with 10% FBS, GlutaMAX and Pen/Strep and passaged upon reaching confluence using Accutase. The PA cells were lentivirally infected to express core histone protein H2B-red fluorescent protein (RFP) under the EF1α promoter (RRID: 201121) within the nucleus, as described below. The cells comprised a mixed population of ∼80% RFP + /20% RFP neg  cells, did not undergo selection to maintain primary PA cell heterogeneity, and were passaged at high density once per week. Some PA cells were maintained as spheroids by passaging and pelleting 30,000 cells at the bottom of low-attachment U-bottom plates, allowing the tumor cells to aggregate overnight prior to maintaining the spheroids in low-attachment containers under static (nonshaking) conditions. Human cerebral organoids Cerebral organoid cultures were generated as described previously ( Anastasaki et al. 2022b ) with minor adaptations. Human NF1 patient-derived iPSCs heterozygous for an  NF1  mutation ( NF1 Y489C/+ ), iPSCs CRISPR–Cas9-engineered to harbor a heterozygous NF1 patient-derived  NF1  mutation ( NF1 C383X/+ ), and an isogenic control line (BJFF.6) were initially expanded on Matrigel-coated T25 flasks and detached using ReLeSR. Embryoid bodies (EBs) were generated by seeding 40,000 live hiPSCs per well into a 96 well low-attachment plate, followed by centrifugation at 300 g  for 3 min to promote cell aggregation. Neural induction was initiated by replacing mTeSR medium with STEMdiff neural induction medium supplemented with 4 ng/mL bFGF and 20 µM ROCK inhibitor. Each well contained 200 µL of media. On day 2, EBs were examined by bright-field microscopy to confirm their formation. The medium was refreshed on day 4 with bFGF and ROCK inhibitor and again on day 7 without supplements. On day 10, EBs were transferred to ultralow-attachment 24 well plates on an orbital shaker at 80 rpm in a humidified incubator at 37°C and 5% CO 2  and maintained in organoid culture media:1:DMEM/F12:neurobasal medium supplemented with antibiotic/antimycotic solution, N-2 supplement, B-27 Plus supplement, GlutaMAX, MEM NEAA (Gibco, Thermo Fisher Scientific), 250 µL of 100 U/mL humulin (in 1 L), and 4 µL of 2-mercaptoethanol (in 1 L; Sigma). After 4 weeks in vitro (WIV), mature cerebral organoids (COs) were collected and fixed in 4% paraformaldehyde overnight at 4°C. Fixed organoids were then washed in PBS and placed in 30% sucrose for 48 h of cryoprotection. To generate frozen sections, COs were placed in a mixture of 1:2 (v/v) Tissue-Tek OCT compound and 30% sucrose in 15 mm × 15 mm × 5 mm plastic molds. Tissues were snap-frozen using a slurry of dry ice and 2-methylbutane. Frozen samples were sectioned at 10 µm thickness using a cryostat, and two sections were mounted per glass slide for analyses. Differentiation and maintenance of induced neural progenitor cells (iNPCs) To induce neural progenitor differentiation, hiPSCs were plated onto poly-L-ornithine-coated (Sigma-Aldrich) and laminin-coated (Fisher Scientific) tissue culture flasks. Cells were initially cultured for 3 days in NPC base media consisting of 50% DMEM/F12 and 50% neurobasal media supplemented with N-2, B-27 Plus, and 2 mM GlutaMAX (Gibco, Thermo Fisher Scientific). During this phase, the medium was supplemented with 10 ng/mL human LIF, 4 µM CHIR99021, 3 µM SB431542, 2 µM dorsomorphin, and 0.1 µM compound E (Stem Cell Technologies) prior to growth for an additional 5 days in the same NPC base medium containing 10 ng/mL LIF, 4 µM CHIR99021, 3 µM SB431542, and 0.1 µM compound E but omitting dorsomorphin. Thereafter, iNPCs were maintained in NPC base medium supplemented with 10 ng/mL LIF, 3 µM CHIR99021, and 2 µM SB431542. The medium was refreshed daily, and cells were passaged as required using Accutase (Stem Cell Technologies) according to the manufacturer's protocol. Lentiviral production and cell transduction Lentiviral particles encoding H2B-RFP under the EF-1α promoter (RRID: 201121) and hM3D(Gq) DREADD receptors under the SYN1 promoter (VectorBuilder VB241016-1583wgf) were generated using a standard third-generation packaging system. Plasmid constructs and packaging vectors were cotransfected into HEK293T cells using Fugene HD (Promega) according to the manufacturer's protocol. Viral supernatants were harvested 48 h after transfection, passed through a 0.45 µm filter, and immediately applied to either patient-derived PA cells or induced neural progenitor cells (iNPCs). Target cells were exposed to viral supernatants for 72 h, after which infection efficiency was assessed by fluorescence microscopy: RFP +  for PA cells and EGFP +  for iNPCs. Transduced cells were maintained in vitro until they were used for coculture with hCOs. PANCO generation Human iPSC-derived cerebral organoids (hCOs) maintained for a minimum of 4 weeks in 24 well ultralow-attachment plates were assessed for neuronal (TUJ1 + ), neural stem cell (SOX2 + ), and astrocytic (GFAP + ) marker expression. WUPA cells previously transduced with RFP-expressing lentivirus were seeded at a density of 10,000–100,000 cells per well in U-bottom 96 well ultralow-attachment plates 1 day prior to incubation with COs. After 24 h, PA cells formed compact spheroids. For optimal PANCO generation, aggregates from 10,000 cells were gently dissociated using a 200 µL pipette tip to produce smaller spheroids (<100 µm in diameter). For coculture experiments, hCOs were resuspended using organoid culture medium, transferred into 96 well plates containing PA spheroids, and incubated for 72 h to facilitate integration. Following this initial period, cocultured assembloids were returned to the 24 well ultralow-attachment plates and maintained under standard culture conditions for an additional 8 weeks. PA integration was monitored weekly by live-cell imaging of RFP +  PA cells within the PANCOs. If PA-RFP +  cells were not observed after 1 week, the coculture procedure was repeated to enhance the likelihood of successful PA cell integration. Integration of hM3D(Gq)-GFP iNPCs into human cerebral organoids Following infection of iPSC-derived NPCs (iNPCs) with hM3D(Gq)-GFP lentiviral particles, the expression efficiency of hM3D(Gq) DREADD receptor (under the SYN1 promoter) expression in iNPCs was assessed by fluorescence. Once GFP-positive cells exceeded 80%, iNPCs were dissociated using Accutase, and live cells were counted. iNPCs were then resuspended in cerebral organoid culture medium and plated at a density of 50,000 cells per well into U-bottom 96 well ultralow-attachment plates 1 h prior to coculture. Once the iNPCs had settled and formed a pellet, hCOs cultured in 24 well plates were gently transferred onto the iNPC pellet. After a 48 h incubation period, iNPC–hCOs were returned to the 24 well plates. Successful integration was monitored by live-cell imaging starting at 1 week after coculture. If integration was not achieved, the coculture procedure was repeated once to improve the rate of successful integration. Sequential integration and DREADD activation in PANCOs Human iNPC-hM3D–PANCOs were generated via sequential integration of PAs in iNPC–hCOs. iNPC–hCOs (2–4 WIV) were cocultured with WUPA cells as described above for PA cells. Functional activation of hM3DGq iNPC-derived cells was initiated 8 weeks after PANCO integration. For DREADD activation, 10 µM clozapine-N-oxide (CNO) was added to the culture medium for 1 h, followed by a medium change and a second 1 h CNO treatment 24 h later. After a second medium change, PANCOs were maintained for an additional 48 h before collection and immunohistochemical analysis. For memantine treatments, PANCOs were pretreated with 10 µM CNO for 1 h, followed by 24 h of recovery. A second 1 h CNO treatment was then applied, followed by 2 µM memantine addition to the media. PANCOs were collected 24 h after memantine treatment following a total treatment duration of 48 h. Mirdametinib and trametinib treatments PANCOs were treated with 0.5–1.5 µM mirdametinib (MedChem Express) and 50 nM trametinib (MedChem Express), with medium replenished daily for a total of 3 days. Treated PANCOs were then collected for histopathological analyses. hCOs were treated with 1 µM mirdametinib for 72 h prior to collection for histopathological analyses. Unlabeled WUPA cell monolayer cultures were treated with 0.1–1.0 µM mirdametinib for 24 h for proliferation assays and Western blot analyses. Immunocytochemistry, immunofluorescence, and immunohistochemistry Adherent WUPA cells were washed and fixed with 4% paraformaldehyde. Fixed cells and frozen sections were permeabilized with 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS for 10 min. After blocking with 10% goat serum, samples were incubated overnight at 4°C with primary antibodies ( Supplemental Table S1 ) diluted in 2% goat serum according to the manufacturer-recommended concentrations. Alexa fluor-conjugated secondary antibodies (1:200) were then applied, and nuclei were counterstained with Hoechst 33258 (Thermo Scientific). Samples were mounted with Immu-Mount (Fisher) and imaged using a Leica DMi1 fluorescence microscope with LAS X. For synapsin-I and bassoon immunostaining, high-resolution confocal imaging was performed using a Zeiss LSM 880 with Airyscan to assess synaptic proximity between integrated neuronal and PA cells. For DAB immunohistochemical staining, frozen tissues were serially sectioned (5 µm) and immunostained with Ki67, GFAP, OLIG2, phospho-ERK1/2, and synaptophysin antibodies ( Supplemental Table S1 ) using the VectaStain ABC kit and the appropriate biotinylated secondary antibodies. Proximity ligation assays Proximity ligation assays (PLAs) were performed to detect protein–protein interactions between PDGFRA:TUJ1, homer::bassoon, homer::PDGFRA, and PDGFRA::bassoon. Each assay was conducted using the Duolink in situ detection kit (Millipore Sigma DUO92013) according to the manufacturer's specifications. Briefly, all reagents were freshly prepared. PANCO tissue cryosections were washed and blocked using Duolink blocking solution, The appropriate primary antibodies ( Supplemental Table S1 ) were diluted 1:100 in Duolink antibody diluent. After the staining was complete, the slides were mounted using Duolink mounting medium containing DAPI before undergoing confocal imaging. Western blotting Treated WUPA cells were collected, snap-frozen, and lysed in protease/phosphatase inhibitor-supplemented RIPA buffer for subsequent Western blotting as described previously ( Anastasaki et al. 2025 ). Briefly, 20 µg of each sample was blotted using pERK1/2, total ERK1/2, and GAPDH primary and appropriate HRP- and NIR-conjugated secondary antibodies ( Supplemental Table S1 ). Images were captured and analyzed using Li-COR Image Studio Lite (version 5.2). Resazurin proliferation assays Thirty-thousand WUPA cells were seeded in each well of a 96 well plate 24 h prior to treatment with vehicle (DMSO) or 0.1–1 µM mirdametinib for a total of 24 h. During the last 6 h of treatment, 10% (v/v) resazurin (Thermo Fisher) was added to each well according to the manufacturer's instructions. Metabolized resazurin produced resorufin as PA cells proliferated. Resorufin fluorescence was analyzed on a Varioskan LUX multimode microplate reader (Thermo Fisher) using SkanIt (Thermo Fisher). Quantification and statistical analyses Statistical analyses were performed using GraphPad Prism 5. Depending on the comparison, either two-tailed Student's  t -tests or one-way ANOVA with Dunnett's or Tukey's post hoc corrections were used. Statistical significance was defined as  P  < 0.05, with exact  P -values reported in the corresponding figure panels. Each analysis included data from a minimum of three independently generated biological replicates. Each biological replicate represented the average of a minimum of two technical replicates.
